issues.legal_issue: Abolition of an intermediary’s estate does not extinguish that person’s separate raiyati interest in a holding, or the person’s interest in buildings standing on that holding.
material_facts: The proprietors had purchased occupancy holdings from raiyats under tenure-holders and were recorded as occupancy raiyats in the settlement records.
Buildings stood on the holdings and were used by the proprietors as offices for administering their estate and for related purposes.
The estate had vested in the State, but the interests of the tenure-holders and sub-proprietors had not been taken over.
State officials took possession of the holdings and buildings.
issues.conclusion: The raiyati interests in the lands and the buildings standing on them were not affected by abolition of the proprietors’ interests in the estate. The State officials’ taking of possession was illegal.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(g) and 2(h) of the Orissa Estates Abolition Act, 1951, an estate comprises intermediary interests between the State and the raiyat; the Act abolishes those intermediary interests but does not affect a raiyat’s holding. Sections 3 and 5 provide for vesting of the estate and its specified interests, while section 26 concerns assessment of compensation and does not make raiyati interests vest in the State. The definition of “homestead” in section 2(i) concerns buildings comprised in the estate, not buildings on raiyati holdings. The holding is the raiyat’s unit of interest under the Orissa Tenancy Act, 1913.

rule.if: estate_vesting_dispute and raiyati_holding_purchased_from_raiyat and occupancy_status_recorded and buildings_stand_on_holding

predicates.estate_vesting_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether property was taken over when an estate vested under an abolition scheme.
predicates.raiyati_holding_purchased_from_raiyat: An intermediary purchased a holding from a raiyat and thereby held that property in the capacity of a raiyat.
predicates.occupancy_status_recorded: The purchaser’s occupancy status in the holding was recorded in the land records.
predicates.buildings_stand_on_holding: Buildings stand on the raiyati holding, even if the intermediary used them to administer the estate.

issues.definition: When an estate-vesting dispute concerns a purchased holding recorded as an occupancy holding with buildings on it, the raiyati interest and the buildings remain outside the estate vesting.

issues.legal_issue: A rule concerning buildings used to administer an estate does not extend to buildings standing on a raiyati holding merely because they served that administrative purpose.
material_facts: The buildings were situated on lands held by the proprietors as occupancy raiyats, rather than on land held by them as proprietors or tenure-holders.
The buildings were used as offices for estate administration and for related purposes.

The High Court relied on observations in an earlier decision concerning buildings used for estate administration; those observations addressed buildings on the proprietor’s private land, not buildings on raiyati land.
issues.conclusion: The earlier decision did not establish that the buildings on the raiyati holdings vested in the State; the High Court’s reliance on it was unfounded.
issues.legal_principle: The observations in K. C. Gajapati Narayan Deo v. State of Orissa, 1954 SCR 1, concerned the treatment of buildings on a proprietor’s private land under the definition of “homestead” in section 2(i) of the Orissa Estates Abolition Act, 1951. They did not concern raiyati lands. The Act’s provisions concerning estate vesting and compensation do not extend that treatment to buildings on a raiyati holding.

predicates.estate_vesting_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether property was taken over when an estate vested under an abolition scheme.
predicates.buildings_stand_on_raiyati_holding: The buildings stand on land held by the person as a raiyat.
predicates.earlier_building_rule_concerned_propriet: The earlier rule addressed buildings on land held in a proprietary or tenure-holder capacity, rather than buildings on a raiyati holding.

issues.definition: When an estate-vesting dispute concerns buildings on a raiyati holding and the earlier building rule concerned proprietary land, that earlier rule does not govern the raiyati buildings.
